changes.comment: Publishes the size a consumer actually ships, and makes the README table generated rather than hand-written. `rush size` now measures every entry twice — once plainly, once with `NODE_ENV` defined as `"production"` — and writes the second figure into the table between the `<!-- size-table:start -->` markers in README.md and README.es.md. The budget stays pinned to the first, larger measurement, so dev-only code still cannot grow unnoticed. `{ createStore }` is 8.3 KB rather than the 9.2 KB previously published: roughly 9% of that gap was development-only guards a production build drops, and the rest the es2022 target. `rushx size` fails when the committed table does not match the measurement, which is the guard the budget alone could never give — the budget answers "has this exploded?", never "is what we tell people true?". The Spanish README gained the per-import table it never had; it previously carried a headline figure with nothing behind it.
